source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A pharmacogenetic crisis triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine in susceptible people","B":"A heat illness caused only by prolonged environmental exposure without any anesthetic trigger","C":"A chronic metabolic disorder that develops gradually over months rather than during anesthesia","D":"An exertional heat illness caused by exercise in hot conditions rather than anesthetic exposure"}}
source_row.rationale: Malignant hyperthermia is specifically triggered by certain anesthetic agents (such as succinylcholine or volatile inhaled anesthetics) in genetically susceptible individuals, typically occurring acutely during or shortly after surgical anesthesia — distinct from heat stroke, which results from environmental heat exposure and/or exertion, though both are hypermetabolic emergencies requiring rapid cooling and supportive treatment.
